chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from al-'Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

That he passed by a group of people eating locusts while they were in the state of Ihram, so he said, 'Glory be to Allah, and you are in Ihram.' They said, 'It is merely the game of the sea.' So he said to them, 'Then throw it into the water.'
And that which indicates that the redemption (fidyah) is obligatory upon him if he eats it is what has been narrated.

key_terms.مُحْرِمُونَ: Those in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj/Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating locusts while in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) clarified the ruling on locusts for those in Ihram, rejecting the argument that they are merely 'sea game' by instructing the eaters to throw them back, thereby signaling the obligation of fidyah. This narration, found in Al-Tusi's *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the scholarly distinction between land and sea game in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that consumption while in a state of ritual consecration incurs a penalty even if the animal itself is permissible.
